name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but 5.9% higher than a year earlier
state: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October, down 1.2% on September but 5.9% above a year earlier (Bizcommunity, 6 Nov). The annual rise meets the Watch line while the index stays below the 135 Alert line. Indian rice exporters were preparing on 6 Nov for possible curbs on broken rice, but no notification had been issued (S&P Global); searches on 27 Nov found no export bans by several major exporters of a staple.
for_you: Households in import-dependent countries and on low incomes are most exposed, as higher world prices for staples tend to reach shop prices with a lag of several months.
rubric_hit: FFPI 133.9 (Oct) in the 120–135 Watch band; y/y +5.9% > +5%

sources.title: Bizcommunity — Global food prices fall in October as sugar rises for fourth month
S&P Global — Indian rice exporters brace for possible curbs on 100% broken WR exports

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
